question.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the osculating plane for the curve $r(t)$ at the point where $t=0,$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2}\,k \\ T(t) & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+\sqrt{3}\,k) \\ N(t) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the unit tangent and the principal normal at the point where $t=0$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡0\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡0\,j+\sqrt{3}\,k)=\frac{1}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k \\ N(0) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡0\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡0\,j=j.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, the position vector of the point where $t=0$ is

$$
p=r(0)=(\operatorname{cos}⁡0+(0)\operatorname{sin}⁡0)\,i+(\operatorname{sin}⁡0-(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡0)\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(0)^{2}\,k=⟨1,0,0⟩.
$$

Now, we need to find a vector that's perpendicular to the osculating plane. To do that, we use the cross product of the unit tangent $T(0)$ and the principal normal $N(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\times N(0) & =(\frac{1}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k)\times j \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,i+\frac{1}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are interested only in the direction of the above vector, let's write our perpendicular vector $n$ as 

$$
n=2\cdot (T(0)\times N(0))=-\sqrt{3}\,i+k=⟨-\sqrt{3},0,1⟩.
$$

Finally, let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ denote the position vector of a point on the osculating plane. Since the plane is perpendicular to $n$ and passes through the tip of the position vector $p$, its Cartesian equation can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}(⟨x,y,z⟩-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-\sqrt{3},0,1⟩ & =⟨1,0,0⟩\cdot ⟨-\sqrt{3},0,1⟩ \\ -\sqrt{3}\cdot x+0\cdot y+1\cdot z & =-\sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3}x-z-\sqrt{3} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
